Earlier results: {prior_results}

This prompt is your whole context: do not open plan, spec or todo files, and perform only the work described here.

Background: in VS Code's Copilot chat a worker keeps a built-in tool only if the selected agent also lists it, so a shell-less conductor leaves its workers able only to read files. The fix starts the parent roles as skills in normal chat. This spike answers three questions and picks the outcome. Change nothing in the repository or in ~/.copilot. Use the probe name ksprobe so no installed agent interferes.

Steps:
1. Make a scratch git repository holding .github/agents/ksprobe.agent.md and .github/skills/ksprobe/SKILL.md.
   - The agent has frontmatter name: ksprobe, a double-quoted description containing a colon followed by a space, tools: [read, agent], user-invocable: false, disable-model-invocation: true, and the body: Reply with exactly: AGENT-RAN
   - The skill has name: ksprobe, a double-quoted description containing a colon followed by a space, and a body telling the model to read ksprobe/references/marker.md and print its contents. Create that file, beside SKILL.md under ksprobe/references/, holding SKILL-REFERENCE-READ.
2. Q1. In that repository run `copilot --agent ksprobe -p "hello" --allow-all-tools`. Pass means the output contains AGENT-RAN. On failure repeat with the disable-model-invocation line removed, and report DISABLE_MODEL_INVOCATION: drop if that passes, otherwise keep.
3. Q2. Copy /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dave--claude-spares-spare-wo45o3/9cf93364-77b2-4d4e-8cb9-a7569a87ac6a/scratchpad/hostrepro/run.mjs into your scratch directory. It drives the Copilot SDK and runtime bundled in VS Code Insiders with VS Code's availableTools list. Add a scenario with select: false, skills: true, available: true, and an added custom agent named ksprobe. Its prompt loads the ksprobe skill with the skill tool, prints what the skill says to print, then dispatches github-devops to run echo SHELL-OK and to create and edit probe.txt. Run it with REPRO_SKILLS set to the scratch .github/skills and REPRO_CWD set to the scratch repository. Pass means the skill loads, SKILL-REFERENCE-READ is printed, and the worker's shell and edit calls succeed. Report RELATIVE_REFERENCE: ok or failed from the printed marker.
4. Q3, only when Q2 fails. Add a scenario that dispatches the hidden ksprobe agent, with a prompt telling it to load the skill with its own name and print its marker. Pass means the marker is printed.
5. Hook payload. Add .github/hooks/probe.json with version: 1 and preToolUse and postToolUse entries whose bash command appends stdin to a log file in your scratch directory. Rerun the Q2 scenario and read the log. Report HOOK_PAYLOAD_SHAPE: local if a runSubagent record has hook_event_name, cli if it has toolName, or none if the hook never fired for a dispatch. Report HOOK_DISPATCH_TOOL: with the tool name, and the argument names that carry the target agent and the prompt.
6. Choose SPIKE_BRANCH: A when Q1 and Q2 pass; B when Q1 fails and Q2 passes; C when Q2 fails and Q3 passes; STOP when Q2 and Q3 both fail.

Command: `copilot --agent ksprobe -p "hello" --allow-all-tools` and `node run.mjs <scenario>`, both run from the scratch directory.

Acceptance criteria: the digest carries Q1: pass|fail, Q2: pass|fail, Q3: pass|fail|not-asked, DISABLE_MODEL_INVOCATION: keep|drop, RELATIVE_REFERENCE: ok|failed, HOOK_PAYLOAD_SHAPE: local|cli|none, HOOK_DISPATCH_TOOL: <name> and SPIKE_BRANCH: A|B|C|STOP, each with its command and output. git status in the repository shows no change from this task.
